description: I'm a physics graduate student at WPI doing this solo for the Cambridge event, interested in the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer and building a simple moon base game on my own.
summary:
I made a little game in PowerPoint called Moonbase in Balance. I teach physics labs at university and wanted to make something the students could actually play and have some fun with rather than just read. 

You're in charge of a small moon base for 5 days in this game. Four astronauts are depending on you. You've got to look after four things: oxygen, water, power and the health of the crew. Every day there's a new problem and you get two options to choose from. I've designed it so that every option has a cost. If you fix one thing, something else will suffer. If anything hits zero you're game over. You win if you get through Day 5 with everything still in the green.
details:
Moonbase in Balance is a small game I made in PowerPoint. You are in charge of a moon base for 5 days and you look after 4 astronauts. Every day something goes wrong. One day there is a dust storm, another day the oxygen recycler stops working. You click A or B and the game takes you to what happens because of your choice.

You have to keep watching 4 things: oxygen, water, power and the health of the crew. They keep going up and down with every choice. If any one of them becomes zero, the mission is over. If all 4 are above 50% on day 5, you win. On the last slide I have asked the player to make their own day 6.

I teach physics labs, and honestly students remember things better when they are playing and deciding themselves. In this game no choice is fully good. If you repair one thing, something else becomes less. I feel that is how real missions also are, everything is limited and you have to balance.

The full game is only in PowerPoint. I used the clickable links between slides for the choices, so anybody can play it on a normal laptop. No app to install, no coding. I kept the words simple so even younger students can play, and one full game takes only a few minutes.
